parsed.refutation_attempt: The sprintf call uses the format string "%06llu" which guarantees a zero‑padded six‑digit output. The argument is `timestamp % 1000000`, which by definition yields a value in the inclusive range 0–999999. Thus the resulting string is always exactly six characters long. Adding the terminating null byte requires a buffer of size 7, which matches the declaration `char microseconds[7];`. There is no control flow that bypasses this check, and the modulo operation ensures the value cannot exceed the range that the format string can produce. Hence the buffer overflow claim is unfounded.
